carryOn.reason: Protein bars, energy bars, granola bars, and all solid food snacks are fully allowed in carry-on baggage by the TSA. They are not subject to the 3-1-1 liquids rule.

international.note: When entering countries like Australia or New Zealand, always declare packaged food items at customs. Most commercially sealed protein bars are permitted, but biosecurity rules apply.

travelTips: Protein bars are one of the best travel snacks — no liquid restrictions, no special handling needed.
Pack several bars in your carry-on to avoid paying airport food prices.
When entering Australia, declare all food items including protein bars at biosecurity — most commercially packaged bars are cleared.

faq.question: Can I bring protein bars in my carry-on bag?
faq.answer: Yes! Protein bars, energy bars, granola bars, and all solid food snacks are fully allowed in carry-on bags. They are not liquids so they are not subject to the TSA 3-1-1 rule. You can bring as many as you like.

faq.question: Can you pack protein bars in checked luggage?
faq.answer: Yes. Protein bars and all packaged solid food are fully allowed in checked bags with no quantity limit.

faq.question: Can I take protein bars through airport security in the UK?
faq.answer: Yes. Protein bars and solid snacks are allowed through airport security in the UK (CAA rules), US (TSA), and throughout Europe (EASA). They are not subject to the 100ml liquids rule.

faq.question: Can I bring protein bars to Australia?
faq.answer: You must declare all food items including protein bars when entering Australia. Most commercially sealed protein bars are cleared by Australian Border Force biosecurity, but they may be inspected. Declare — don't conceal.
